data.title: Russia, Ukraine launch overnight strikes on each other's oil infrastructure after Trump's claim
data.description:
Russia and Ukraine carried out aerial strikes on each other's energy infrastructure overnight Tuesday, despite President Trump's claim that both sides had agreed to stop hitting energy targets.

Ukraine ​hit the Syzran oil refinery in southern Russia and a drone production facility after Ukraine's President Zelensky said Russia "continues to attack our energy sector, regular logistics, and critical infrastructure," without elaborating; other officials said Russia had targeted gasoline stations in Kyiv and unspecified energy infrastructure in the southeastern Zaporizhzhia region.

Zelenskyy had said Ukraine was ready to halt such strikes but required credible guarantees from its partners that Russia would also ​stop, and a Kremlin spokesperson said Trump's suggestion was "a ⁠good initiative" but Western countries needed to lift sanctions against Russia and "unlawful restrictions on energy supplies."

Trump, under political pressure from rising fuel prices in the U.S., had said he told Zelenskyy that Ukraine needs to stop hitting diesel fuel in Russia.

The average price of a gallon of diesel in the U.S. hit a fresh record high of $6.27 on Tuesday, compared to $3.69/gal a year ago, according to the American Automobile Association.

Three of Russia's six top ​diesel-producing refineries were forced to significantly cut back or completely halt output in September due to ‌damage sustained in drone attacks, Reuters reported, citing calculations based on data from fuel market participants.

Crude oil futures continued to rise Tuesday as the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's critical East-West Pipeline and recent territorial gains by Houthi militants in Yemen have heightened worries over Middle East crude supplies.

Front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for October delivery jumped 2.3% to $103.76/bbl, front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for November delivery climbed 2% to $107.82/bbl.

data.title: FHFA's Pulte highlights growing market share of VantageScore in latest X posts
data.description:
U.S. Federal Housing Director Bill Pulte highlighted the growing market share of VantageScore relative to FICO score in his X posts.

Last week, Pulte said in a social media post that all mortgage-backed securities, credit risk transfers, and securitized products issued by Fannie Mae (FNMA) and Freddie Mac (FMCC) will now carry a VantageScore in addition to a FICO score.

VantageScore is an independent joint venture company owned by Equifax (EFX), Experian (EXPGF) (EXPGY), and TransUnion (TRU).

Pulte, who chairs Fannie Mae (FNMA)/Freddie Mac (FMCC), has repeatedly criticized the scoring solutions and services provider, Fair Isaac (FICO), as a monopoly and pushed for the use of VantageScore by lenders.

FICO is said to be used by 90% of lenders.

In his latest X post, Pulte said, "A small amount of biased people cast doubt that the market would welcome two (plus?) predictive credit scores, but per Bloomberg Terminal, the second score is strongly competing at 13% market share."

"Mortgage spreads are super tight. I expect the percentage to go higher and competition to go up."

"In another pool, VantageScore is at 59% market share while FICO is at 40% market share," he said separately.  "Competition is good. Let them compete!"

data.title: Vera Bradley reiterates $255M-$270M FY2027 sales outlook while targeting at least 50% operating profit improvement
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Vera Bradley (VRA) Q2 fiscal 2027

Management view

  • CEO & Chairman of the Board Ian Bickley framed Q2 as “another strong quarter,” saying the company delivered “our second consecutive quarter of overall growth with total revenue up 1.1% versus the prior year,” while acknowledging the pace was “more modest than the nearly 8% we delivered last quarter.”

  • Bickley highlighted balance sheet and cash flow progress, stating, “Inventory ended the quarter down 28% compared to the second quarter last year,” and “we generated $23 million of operating cash flow in the period,” adding the company ended with “$34 million of cash… and no debt.”

  • Bickley emphasized channel mix and the deliberate reset of Indirect, saying, “Our Direct segment delivered revenue growth of 8% versus the prior year,” while “in our Indirect channel segment… revenue contracted 39% compared to the prior year” due to “intentional shifts in timing… and reduction in liquidation sales.”

  • Bickley detailed product and collaboration performance, calling out that “Hello Kitty was a standout,” that “the reintroduction of Winnie the Pooh… continued to perform well,” and that in outlet “our Star Wars Droid collaboration performed well,” while also noting ongoing traction from “Stitch and Honeydukes IP product” and “the successful return of Vera Originals.”

  • Bickley disclosed a wholesale go-to-market change: “we recently made the decision to reestablish our in-house sales team to accelerate growth while discontinuing our previous arrangement with a third-party sales representative agency.”

  • CFO & COO Martin Layding said, “For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, our consolidated revenues totaled $71.6 million,” and reported “net income from continuing operations… $3.3 million or $0.11 per diluted share.”

Outlook

  • Layding reiterated full-year guidance: “For fiscal 2027, we are reiterating our prior guidance, including sales in the range of $255 million to $270 million and a year-over-year operating profit improvement of at least 50%.”

  • Management’s framing of the year’s operating improvement remained consistent with Q1’s raised expectation; Bickley said, “we continue to expect our year-over-year non-GAAP operating loss improvement to be at least 50%, consistent with the guidance we shared last quarter,” while also pointing to “strategic shifts in our marketplace strategy while reducing liquidation sales.”

Financial results

  • Layding attributed a major gross margin rate swing to refunds: “During the quarter, we received $8 million in tariff refunds net of interest,” adding that “tariff refunds drove approximately 980 basis points of gross profit rate increase year-to-year.”

  • Layding reported gross profit of “$42.8 million or 59.8% of net revenues,” and explained that excluding tariff refunds, “underlying Q2 gross margin… improved more than 40 basis points versus last year,” driven by “product margin improvement and freight efficiencies,” partially offset by “margin pressure as we strategically cleared through non-go-forward Project Restoration product.”

  • Layding reported SG&A of “$38.7 million or 54% of net revenues,” saying the increase was “primarily due to increased variable compensation expenses,” and lapping “last year’s Q2 stock forfeitures associated with senior leadership changes.”

  • Layding said Q2 operating income from continuing operations was “$4.3 million or 5.9% of net revenues,” and cited liquidity and working capital progress with “cash and cash equivalents… $34.2 million,” “no borrowings on our ABL facility,” and inventory of “$69.3 million,” including mention of “the $5.3 million Project Restoration inventory reserve.”

Q&A

  • Eric Beder, Small Cap Consumer Research, LLC asked how to think about inventory as the company anniversaries sell-through and reserves; CFO Layding responded, “inventory will continue to decline through the end of the year,” with “some small increase” next year alongside growth, and said the focus is “continued turn improvement… into the 2 to 3 range.”

  • Beder asked where management sees encouragement in Indirect and what changes with moving from third-party to direct selling; CEO Bickley answered that specialty and department store wholesale showed “mid-single-digit sell-in growth,” and said the Indirect reset includes rebuilding “our in-house sales team,” focusing on “strategic accounts,” “reducing liquidation,” and optimizing the “marketplace portfolio” where some platforms “may be managed as wholesale accounts” or “as direct accounts.”

  • Beder asked for Back to School learnings; CEO Bickley said the occasion is one Vera Bradley “really can own,” added the team was “very pleased with the preparation,” and cited a miss: “there were several prints in which we had the backpacks, but then not the matchback lunch bags.”

  • Beder asked how to think about holiday product and flows now that the assortment is fully controlled; CEO Bickley said, “we are now 100% in control of the assortment and the buys,” and added the company feels “very confident about the assortment,” particularly “the accessories and small bags.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts were positive and constructive, opening with “Congratulations on another solid quarter,” while focusing questions on sustainability of inventory reductions, rebuilding Indirect, and execution details for Back to School and holiday.

  • Management’s tone was confident in execution and control, using phrases like “we remain confident in the path forward” (CEO Bickley) and “we are encouraged by the progress” (CFO Layding), while acknowledging trade-offs in Indirect tied to “strategic shifts” and reduced liquidation.

  • Versus Q1, management maintained a similar optimistic posture on the transformation but discussed a more uneven channel picture, with Q2 Indirect contraction contrasted with Q1’s Indirect growth narrative tied to collaborations and timing.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q2 kept the same full-year targets as Q1, with Layding reiterating “sales in the range of $255 million to $270 million” and “operating profit improvement of at least 50%,” consistent with Q1’s raise to “at least 50% from 40%.”

  • The channel story shifted: Q1 highlighted Indirect growth supported by “strategic collaborations… including Target,” while Q2 described Indirect down 39% due to “marketplace strategy” timing and “reduction in liquidation sales,” alongside stronger Direct momentum.

  • Strategic actions evolved, with Q2 adding a concrete wholesale operating change to “reestablish our in-house sales team,” while Q1 emphasized leadership additions (including the head of digital commerce) and Outlet 2.0 expansion plans.

Risks and concerns

  • Management cited operational and margin balancing pressures from clearing legacy goods; Layding noted “margin pressure as we strategically cleared through non-go-forward Project Restoration product,” while Bickley said the company is “past the halfway point on working through our legacy inventory.”

  • The Indirect reset and marketplace approach remains a swing factor, with Bickley describing the need to “reset our Indirect business and set it up for long-term… growth,” including reduced liquidation and different operating models by platform.

  • Store footprint changes affected growth rates; Layding said having “14 fewer stores open in Q2… reduced total growth by approximately 100 basis points.”

Final takeaway

Management described Q2 as a second consecutive growth quarter led by stronger Direct comps, margin expansion aided by an $8 million tariff refund, and improved liquidity with $34.2 million in cash and no debt. Leadership reiterated FY2027 guidance of $255 million to $270 million in sales and at least 50% operating profit improvement, while outlining a more deliberate Indirect rebuild—reducing liquidation, optimizing marketplace participation, and reestablishing an in-house sales team—alongside continued emphasis on disciplined promotions, inventory turns, and Back to School and holiday execution.

data.title: Meta plans wider use of in-house AI chips as it targets lower costs
data.description:
Meta Platforms (META) plans to put a new generation of its internally designed artificial intelligence chips into data centers in the first half of next year, with the company targeting lower energy use and costs for running AI models.

The third-generation processor, MTIA 450, code-named Arke, is currently being tested, while its successor, MTIA 500, or Astrid, is expected to complete design work in about a month and enter data centers by the end of 2027, Yee Jiun Song, Meta's VP of engineering, said in an interview with Bloomberg.

“Each one takes on a little bit more risk technologically and gets us better performance,” Song said, referring to the progression of Meta's (META) custom chips. He said that includes better performance per watt and per dollar.

The Facebook parent is working with Broadcom (AVGO) on chip designs and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) on production. The company has committed to more than a gigawatt of the chips over a 12-month period, Song said, adding that it expects deployment to accelerate afterward if AI demand remains strong.

Twelve Arke chips arrived from TSMC (TSM) on September 1, with performance within 2% to 3% of simulations. The processors have already run Meta (META) models as well as models from DeepSeek (DEEPSEEK) and Alibaba (BABA), Song said.

Meta (META) canceled its planned Olympus chip, which was intended for both AI training and inference, partly because of cost concerns. The company is instead focusing on inference.

“These are the workhorse chips that we’re going to use for general-purpose inference,” Song said.

The company expects future chip generations to improve speed and throughput, with Song saying Meta (META) has “a very robust roadmap” for custom silicon.

data.title: GSK upgraded at Berenberg on growth outlook
data.description:
Berenberg upgraded GSK (GSK) to Buy From Hold, saying the company is undervalued and its "heavy discount to peers is no longer justified."

The firm increased its price target to £22 from £20 (~19% upside based on Sept. 14 close on the London Stock Exchange).

Analyst Kerry Holford said that while GSK's HIV franchise will begin to experience patent expirations in 2028, its cost savings program will support R&D and better margins.

She also highlighted upcoming pipeline catalysts, such as potential US approval of bepirovirsen for hepatitis B and neladalkib for second-line non-small cell lung cancer by the end of the year.

Within the next year, pipeline readouts include phase 3 data for the antibody-drug conjugate risvutatug rezetecan (ris-rez) in second-line small-cell lung cancer; every four month Cabenuva (cabotegravir) for HIV; and proof-of-concept data for the long-acting anti-TSLP felcorekibart for asthma.

Berenberg projects 2031 group sales of ~£39B (consensus is ~£36B).

"Recently launched assets (Exdensur, Blenrep) will contribute to growth over this time-period," Holford wrote. "The opportunity for bepirovirsen, the Nuvalent lung cancer assets and GSK/Hansoh oncology ADCs is underappreciated, in our view."

data.title: Guggenheim turns bullish on defense stocks, warns on aerospace aftermarket
data.description:
Guggenheim Securities launched coverage of 22 aerospace and defense companies with a bullish view of defense contractors and aircraft manufacturers. The firm is more cautious about commercial aerospace aftermarket suppliers as passenger traffic weakens and airlines face higher fuel costs.

The analysts said defense stocks have fallen about 25% from their March 2026 peak, while forward valuation multiples have contracted roughly 55%. Guggenheim views the decline as a buying opportunity because geopolitical threats, weapons replenishment and military modernization should support spending into the next decade.

$1 trillion budget could support growth

The firm expects the fiscal 2027 base defense budget to reach approximately $1 trillion. Investment accounts could approach $600 billion, or more than 43% of total defense spending. That compares with 32% in fiscal 2013.

For investors, the central argument is that defense companies now combine lower valuations with unusually strong revenue visibility. Publicly traded contractors’ backlogs rose 25% from a year earlier during the second quarter and 42% from the second quarter of 2024, according to Guggenheim. Expansion of manufacturing capacity could also accelerate sales as contractors replenish missile inventories and deploy newer technologies.

Guggenheim initiated Buy ratings on Applied Aerospace & Defense (AADX), BWX Technologies (BWXT), Curtiss-Wright (CW), Leonardo DRS (DRS), Karman Holdings (KRMN), Kratos Defense (KTOS), L3Harris Technologies (LHX), Lyntris (LYNX), Mercury Systems (MRCY) and Northrop Grumman (NOC). The analysts’ price targets imply average upside of about 38%.

Applied Aerospace (AADX) carries the largest projected return, with a $30 target that represents 143% upside from the price cited in the report. Other notable calls include Karman (KRMN), with 79% potential upside, Lyntris (LYNX) with 60% and Kratos (KTOS) with 58%. Guggenheim rated Moog (MOG.A)(MOG.B), Redwire (RDW) and York Space Systems (YSS) as Neutral.

L3Harris offers a restructuring opportunity

L3Harris (LHX) is Guggenheim’s differentiated large-cap recommendation. The firm assigned the company a $365 price target, implying 49% upside from the report’s reference price of $246. Guggenheim believes asset sales, business separations and industry consolidation could unlock value beyond the benefits of higher defense spending.

The analysts acknowledged several risks to their defense thesis. These include the November elections, the federal deficit, higher interest rates and uncertainty surrounding supplemental spending. A continuing resolution also funds the government only through Dec. 11, leaving major budget decisions until after the elections.

Aircraft production and aftermarket prospects diverge

Guggenheim is also bullish on suppliers tied to new aircraft production. It expects Boeing (BA) production to grow at an 11% compound annual rate through 2030, including 15% growth for wide-body aircraft and 10% for narrow-body jets. The firm rates Howmet Aerospace (HWM), Hexcel (HXL), RBC Bearings (RBC) and Woodward (WWD) as Buy, with average potential upside of 31%.

The outlook is less favorable for aftermarket companies. Guggenheim forecasts global passenger traffic growth of only 1.8% in 2026, down from 5.4% last year. Higher fares, slower traffic and additional aircraft retirements could weaken parts demand within six to 12 months. The firm initiated Neutral ratings on AAR (AAR), Heico (HEI), StandardAero (SARO), TransDigm (TDG) and VSE (VSEC).

data.title: Tenet Healthcare slips after $2.6M insider sale
data.description:
• Tenet Healthcare (THC) traded lower as markets opened Tuesday after Richard Mark, one of its directors, disclosed the sale of more than $2.6M worth of shares of the hospital operator.
  • In a regulatory filing on Monday, Mark reported selling 10K shares of Tenet Healthcare (THC) for an average price of $263.42 each. The transaction, worth $2.63M, took place on Thursday, cutting his ownership in Tenet (THC) by roughly 28% to about 25.1K shares.
  • His divestment comes as the Dallas, Texas-based firm trades nearly 40% above its year-ago level.  
  • Wall Street has remained bullish on Tenet (THC) stock, with an average rating of Strong Buy from analysts, while Seeking Alpha authors indicate THC as a Buy. However, SA’s Quant System, which consistently beats the market, rates THC as a Hold.

data.title: Silver Lake, Intel-backed Altera files confidentially for IPO
data.description:
Silver Lake and Intel-backed chipmaker Altera has confidentially filed for an initial public offering.

The company has not yet disclosed the size of the offering or a price range, according to an announcement Tuesday. An earlier Reuters report indicated that the company could raise more than $2B in the offering.

Altera develops programmable chips used in areas including artificial intelligence, industrial automation, and robotics. Last April Intel (INTC) agreed to sell 51% of its stake in Altera to Silver Lake.

According to a previous report, Silver Lake has hired Barclays (BCS), Citi (C), JPMorgan (JPM), and Morgan Stanley (MS) as underwriters for the IPO.

data.title: Pre-midterm rate hike bets double as policy too stimulative – BofA survey
data.description:
Instituional investor expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike before the November U.S. midterm elections have surged, according to the latest Bank of America Global Fund Manager Survey.

The September survey revealed that 41% of fund managers now expect the Fed to raise rates before the midterms, up sharply from 22% in August.

Over the same period, the proportion of investors confident that the central bank will refrain from hiking dropped to 52% from 72%.

 

The hawkish shift mirrors broader market positioning ahead of the central bank's decision on Wednesday, with data from CME FedWatch indicating a 92% market-implied probability of a rate hike, up from around 60% just a week earlier. These soaring hike expectations are primarily driven by sticky inflation remaining well above the 2% target and surprisingly robust August payroll data.

Adding to pressures on Fed tightening, fund managers noted growing unease over current financial conditions. A net 25% of surveyed investors stated that global monetary policy is currently "too stimulative," marking the highest level for this metric since September 2022.

data.title: Netskope receives Overweight rating due to durable 20%-plus growth: Stephens
data.description:
Stephens initiated coverage on Netskope (NTSK) with an Overweight rating due in part to its position in the Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, and its ability to sustain healthy top-line growth.

"We believe that Netskope has established itself as a leader in SASE with a differentiated offering and is well-positioned to deliver durable 20%+ top-line growth complemented by margin expansion," said Stephens analyst Todd Weller in an investor report. "We believe that recent solid F2Q27 results should serve to increase confidence in the fundamental story. If Netskope can deliver similarly strong performance in 2H FY27, we believe this should be a positive catalyst for the stock through both upside to estimates and multiple expansion."

Netskope made its initial public offering exactly one year ago. Stephens set a $21 price target on the stock. It has surpassed estimates in all four of its public earnings results, including its most recent, which was the second quarter of fiscal 2027. 

"Netskope has established itself as a leader in SASE and in the SSE component of SASE, as validated by leading industry analysts," Weller noted. "We believe that Netskope has a strong and differentiated technology approach that includes its ability to deeply inspect modern cloud, API, and AI traffic, strong data security capabilities, and a high-performance SASE network."

Stephens expects Netskope's full-year fiscal 2027 annual recurring revenue to reach $1.01B, revenue of $890M and an adjusted earnings per share of ($0.15). For fiscal 2028, it expects the cybersecurity company to report ARR of $1.23B, revenue of $1.08B and adjusted EPS of $0.03.
